text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
- Economy Minister Augusto Mateus will renew efforts to find a carmaker willing to take over a state controlled factory in Setubal that produces Renault Clio saloons.
- 1996 profits of banks belonging to businessman Antonio Champalimaud were in line with expectations.
- Portugal will invest 100 billion escudos in port infrastructures by the end of the century, according to a white paper presented by the government today.
- Prizes from Portuguese lotteries will rise by 15 percent this year.
- Luis Filipe Madeira was invited by Prime Minister Antonio Guterres to be leader of the Socialist Party parliamentary group.
- Port authorities at Lisbon, Setubal, Leixoes and Sines will be converted into public companies.
- Portugal's birth rate rose in 1996, compared with 1995, the first increase since the 1970s.
- Railway workers called a strike between 0600 and 2400 today to press for higher salaries and improvements in career structures.
